instrument.title: NIAR Agency Readiness Scorecard
instrument.subtitle: National Infrastructure Asset Repository — Barbados
instrument.notes: Operationalises Step 1 of the Agency Onboarding Procedure (Annex 1, Table 7). Scores are never displayed to respondents.

welcome.heading: NIAR Agency Readiness Scorecard
body: Thank you for taking part. This short assessment helps us understand how your agency works with its information today, so that NIAR can be built around what you actually do rather than around assumptions.
This is not an audit and no agency is being ranked. There are no right or wrong answers — the most useful answer is the honest one.
It takes about 12 minutes. Please choose the description that best matches how your team works on a normal week.
welcome.consent_note: Your individual answers are used only to build your agency's profile and are reported in aggregate.

scale.reference: Digital Maturity Assessment, Table 16 — Digital Maturity Spectrum (0–5)

scoring.dimension_score: unweighted mean of the item scores assigned to that dimension
scoring.agency_score: unweighted mean of the eight dimension scores
scoring.baseline_label: NIAR ecosystem baseline — Emerging Federated Stage

blocks.intro: A few details so we can read the results properly.

questions.prompt: Agency
Your name

questions.prompt: Which best describes your role?
How do you work with your agency's information?

options.label: I use it to make decisions
I manage the team that does

questions.prompt: How long have you worked at this agency?

blocks.title: Your systems and data
blocks.intro: These questions describe the tools and information your agency works with today.

questions.prompt: Does your agency collect geospatial data?

options.label: Secondary data
options.note: We use data produced by others

questions.prompt: Does your agency run any of the following systems?

options.label: ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning tool — e.g. SAP)

questions.reconciliation_note: Presented verbatim to preserve comparability with the 13 agencies already surveyed. Authoring stack and operational systems are separated downstream via tags, not in the respondent-facing list. DMS is present here but absent from Annex 1 Table 1 — review the existing 13 responses for unreported DMS data.

questions.prompt: Which geospatial data formats does your agency use?
questions.reconciliation_note: Verbatim. Annex 1 Table 2 percentages derive from this exact option set — do not modify.

questions.prompt: Do you also use any of these?
questions.help: Select all that apply. Leave blank if none.

options.label: A database that is not geospatial (e.g. Access, SQL)

questions.reconciliation_note: Additive set, kept separate from B3 so that the historical percentage comparison against the 13 agencies remains clean.

questions.prompt: Roughly how much of your key information exists only on paper?
questions.reconciliation_note: Key addition. The original instrument captured the presence of paper but never its volume, which is what determines Tier D assignment and the sizing of the Digitization Sub-Layer.

questions.prompt: Does your agency use GPS data collecting equipment?
Which GPS devices are used?
Which coordinate system do you normally use?
questions.help: If you are not sure, that is completely fine — "Not sure" is a genuinely useful answer for us.

options.label: Different ones depending on the dataset

questions.open_item: Confirm the national CRS and its EPSG code with Lands & Surveys before the standardisation phase; present the confirmed value first in the list. Does not block deployment.
questions.facilitator_note: This item measures awareness, not ground truth — authoritative CRS is read from the files themselves (.prj, geodatabase definition) at onboarding. Dispersion across respondents in the same agency is the signal: it indicates no declared internal convention and predicts V2 gate failures. In the room, do not ask which CRS they use; ask whether anyone has had a layer from another agency fail to line up where it should.

questions.prompt: How often is your main information updated?

options.label: Only when a project requires it

questions.prompt: Could another agency obtain your data today?

options.label: Yes — it is published online and they can access it
Yes — but we must export it and send it

questions.prompt: Do you hold information that could not be shared openly?

options.label: Data owned by a third party

blocks.title: How your team works today
blocks.intro: For each question, choose the description that most resembles how your team works on a normal week. There are no right answers.

questions.prompt: Where does your team's main information live?

options.label: On individual computers or USB drives
On a shared folder or network drive
In a managed database or geodatabase used by the whole team
On an enterprise platform with backup and defined administration
On an enterprise or cloud platform with monitoring, backup and documented recovery

questions.prompt: If your main system stopped working tomorrow, what would happen?

options.label: We would lose information — there is no copy
Someone probably has a copy somewhere
We make copies from time to time, manually
Backups run automatically and we know where they are
Backups are automatic and we have tested restoring them
We have a tested recovery plan with a defined recovery time

questions.prompt: How do you usually share data with another agency?

options.label: A shared drive or file transfer service
An online map service others can connect to
A service or API that other systems read automatically

questions.prompt: When you receive data from another agency, how much work is needed before you can use it?

options.label: We cannot use it at all
A great deal — we retype or redraw it
Significant — we reformat and correct fields by hand
Some — a known conversion we do routinely
None — it loads directly into our system

questions.prompt: Do the field names and codes in your datasets follow a written standard?

options.label: No — each person names things their own way
There is a habit, but nothing written down
One or two datasets follow an internal convention
We have a written internal standard for our main datasets
Our standard is aligned with a national or international one
Compliance is checked automatically before publishing

questions.prompt: Who checks that the data is correct before it is used or shared?

options.label: The person who made it, informally
A colleague reviews it when there is time
A named person reviews it as part of the process
We apply a checklist or set of rules to every dataset
Automated validation rules run and errors are logged

questions.prompt: If two versions of the same dataset exist, how do you know which one is correct?

options.label: The file name or date tells us
There is one agreed master location
Versioning is controlled by the system
Version history and changes are fully traceable

questions.prompt: How complete is your information about the assets you are responsible for?

options.label: We do not have an inventory
Most assets, with gaps we are aware of
Complete for our main assets, updated periodically
Complete and updated on a defined cycle
Complete, updated, and measured with quality indicators

questions.prompt: When you share a dataset, what travels with it?

options.label: Nothing — the file as it is
The file name and a short note in the email
An internal document explaining the fields
A standard description form completed for every dataset
A description record published in a catalogue others can search
Descriptions generated automatically and audited periodically

questions.prompt: Could a new member of staff find and understand your datasets without asking a colleague?

options.label: No — everything is in people's heads
Only with a great deal of help
Main datasets are documented and kept in a known place
There is a catalogue with descriptions and named owners
The catalogue is searchable, maintained and used daily

questions.prompt: How is access to your information controlled?

options.label: Anyone in the office can open anything
Files sit on a shared drive with no specific rules
Access is granted by role and requested formally
Access is managed by the system with individual accounts and logs
Access is reviewed periodically and audited

questions.prompt: Has your agency classified which information is open, restricted or confidential?

options.label: We know informally which information is sensitive
There is a written classification for our main datasets
Classification is applied to every dataset and enforced by the system
Classification is enforced, audited and reviewed

questions.prompt: Is the procedure for updating your data written down?

options.label: No — each person does it their own way
It is known by the people who do it
The procedure is documented and followed consistently
The procedure is documented, measured and improved

questions.prompt: How do you know when your data is out of date?

options.label: We check when a request comes in
We review it on a schedule
The system shows the last update date for every dataset
We track freshness indicators and act on them

questions.prompt: Is there a person formally responsible for your agency's data?

options.label: Someone does it informally, on top of their own job
It is understood who it is, but not written anywhere
The responsibility is written into someone's role
There is a named data owner and steward with defined duties
Roles are defined, staffed and reviewed

questions.prompt: If the person who mainly handles your GIS or data work left tomorrow, what would happen?

options.label: Major disruption — we would have to rebuild the knowledge
Another person is trained to cover
The work is shared across a team
There is a documented team structure with defined backups

blocks.title: In your own words
blocks.intro: Two open questions. These are the most useful answers you can give us — and you are welcome to finish them together in the session.

questions.prompt: List your existing geospatial datasets.
questions.placeholder:
For example:
1. Roads
2. Coastline
3. Drainage wells
questions.facilitator_note: Display live on the facilitator screen during the session and ask the room what is missing. Reliably surfaces datasets no single respondent listed alone.

questions.prompt: From NIAR, what three questions would you most like answered?
questions.placeholder:
For example:
1. Where are the water hydrants?
2. What is the size of this agricultural plot?
3. Where is the natural gas valve?

questions.prompt: What is the one thing that would make sharing your data with NIAR easier for your team?
questions.pairing_note: D2 captures what the agency gains; D3 captures what NIAR needs from them. Together they form the reciprocity exchange identified in Change Readiness Finding 1 as essential for private sector engagement.

integration_tier.reference: TO-BE Table 10 — Integration Tiers and Method
integration_tier.note: An agency may hold a primary and a secondary tier. Evaluate all rules and record every match; do not collapse to a single value artificially.

rules.label: Assisted Digitization
rules.condition: B4 in ['half','most','almost_all'] OR (B3 includes 'paper_based' AND B4 == 'some')
rules.implication: Field Capacity Team deployment and Digitization Sub-Layer required before any integration pipeline

rules.label: Direct ArcGIS Online Publication
rules.condition: B2 includes any of ['arcgis_online','arcgis_enterprise'] AND B9 == 'published'
rules.implication: Federated catalog harvest via ArcGIS Hub from day one

rules.label: File-Based Submission Portal
rules.implication: Submission Portal upload, staged and processed by the Orchestration Layer

validation_gate_risk.reference: Annex 1 Table 4 — Validation and Quality Control Pipeline

gates.risk_signal: B7 in ['varies','not_sure'] OR B6 includes 'tablet_phone' only
C12 <= 2 AND B10 includes any restricted classification

preprocessing_requirements.trigger: B2 includes 'arcmap' AND not B2 includes 'arcgis_enterprise'

readings.label: Optimism Gap
readings.condition: mean(leadership) - mean(operational) >= 1.5 on the same dimension
readings.interpretation: Not a data problem — a management visibility problem.
readings.probe_template: Leadership sees this working better than the people doing it daily. Can someone walk us through what actually happens on a normal week?

readings.label: Hidden Capability
readings.condition: mean(operational) - mean(leadership) >= 1.5 on the same dimension
readings.interpretation: Capability exists but is not recognised or resourced.
readings.probe_template: The team is doing more here than is visible upstairs. What would it take to make this official?

readings.label: No shared definition
readings.condition: max(scores) - min(scores) >= 2 on the same item
readings.interpretation: No shared internal definition of the practice. Predicts inconsistent submissions.
readings.probe_template: We have very different answers on this one. Can someone show us a concrete recent example?

readings.label: Position against the ecosystem
readings.interpretation: Positions the agency without ranking it.
readings.probe_template: This sits well away from where most agencies are. What explains the difference here?

closing.heading: Thank you
closing.body: Your responses are already feeding into your agency's profile. We will look at the results together in a moment — including where answers in this room differ from one another, which is usually the most interesting part of the conversation.
